whereby the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at 6% per annum in favour of the claimant for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident, whereas the claimant filed MACMA.No.115 of 2019 seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: The brief facts, in nutshell, are that the claimant filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.24,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident that occurred on 08.02.2013.

It is his case that while he was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle, the rider drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly applied brakes, as a result of which both fell down and the claimant sustained grievous head injury,
including multiple haemorrhagic contusions and neurological disability.
He was initially treated at Gandhi Hospital and later at Axon Hospital, Kukatpally.

The Tribunal, upon appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle and awarded a total compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at 6% per annum.
Aggrieved thereby, both the claimant and the Insurance Company preferred the present appeals.

4. Considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

As regards negligence, the Tribunal, on the basis of the evidence of P.W.1 coupled with Ex.A-1 FIR and Ex.A-2 charge sheet, has categorically held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle.
The Insurance Company has not placed any cogent evidence to rebut the said finding.
Though a contention is raised that the claimant was under the influence of alcohol, no material is produced to establish that he was intoxicated at the time of accident.
Mere reference in medical record that the claimant was a chronic alcoholic cannot lead to an inference that he was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident.
In the absence of any contra evidence, this Court finds no reason to interfere with the finding recorded by the Tribunal on negligence.
6. Coming to the quantum of compensation, it is not in dispute that the claimant sustained grievous head injury and suffered neurological disability assessed at 50% by P.W.3-doctor.

The Tribunal,
taking into consideration the nature of avocation of the claimant as a carpenter, rightly treated the functional disability as 100%.
The monthly income of the claimant was taken at Rs.7,758/-, which appears to be reasonable in the absence of strict proof and the same is confirmed.

However, the Tribunal applied multiplier '12', whereas as per settled law, for the age group of the claimant, the appropriate multiplier is '13' and thus the claimant is entitled for Rs.12,10,248/- (Rs.7,758/- X 12 X 13) towards disability.
Further, the amount awarded by the Tribunal towards grievous injuries is found to be on the lower side.
Considering the nature of injuries, the same is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.
Similarly, the amount awarded towards pain and suffering is also inadequate and the same is enhanced to Rs.3,00,000/-.
The compensation awarded towards transportation and extra nourishment is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
Insofar as the medical expenses are concerned, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.1,54,539/- based on the bills and evidence on record.
As the same is supported by documentary evidence, it does not warrant any interference and is accordingly confirmed.

Thus, on an overall consideration of the material on record, this Court is of the opinion that the claimant is entitled to a total enhanced compensation of Rs.17,84,787/- (Rs.12,10,248/- +
Rs.1,00,000/- + Rs.3,00,000/- + Rs.20,000/- + Rs.1,54,539/-), which is rounded off to Rs.17,85,000/-.

sentences.text: Coming to the rate of interest, this Court finds force in the submission of the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Insurance Company.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Mannat Johal and others1 and in several subsequent decisions held that the reasonable rate of interest to be awarded in motor accident claim cases shall be 7.5% per annum.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Mannat Johal and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 6% per annum is on the lower side and requires enhancement.

Resultantly, MACMA.No.23 of 2019 filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed and MACMA.No.115 of 2019 filed by the claimant is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation granted by the Tribunal from Rs.15,00,000/- to Rs.17,85,000/- with interest @ 7.5% from the date of petition till realization.
The remaining terms and conditions of the Tribunal shall stand unaltered.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
